creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Each of these replaces a shipped workaround rather than a hypothetical one. The 2026-07-08 commit (`f69ebced`) already ran this loop once; its message says it fills gaps that forced real scripts to shell out. This is the same loop against a larger corpus.

Ranked by how much they delete:

- `get_cwd` - `bro:65` shells `pwd`; `mci:51` reads `get_env("PWD")`
- `script_path()` / `script_dir()` - `msh:227-229` shells `dirname "$(realpath ...)"`; makes the `../resources` convention work with `read_file`
- `temp_file` / `temp_dir` - `devenv:253`, `laptop:78`, `msh:201`, `jmx:99`
- clipboard get and set - five scripts; `jmx:113-115` is macOS-only inside a team-shared script
- `move_path` / `copy_path` - `tm`, whose entire job is moving files, shells `mv -f`; also `fr:234`, `dot:55`, `sc:39-41`
- `stem` / `extension` on `get_path` - hand-rolled three ways at `imgconvert:40`, `trim:26-28`, `sip:20`
- order-preserving `to_json` - maps already preserve insertion order internally (`core/type_map.go`); only the serializer alphabetizes, and `cct` shells to `jq` because of it
- `find(list, fn)` - `rdbid:24-28`, `posmov:72-76`
- `chr` / `ord` - `asci` is a 130-line codepoint map
- `median` / `percentile` - `promq:130-132` hand-computes next to builtin `min`/`max`/`sum`
- `replace_in_file` with a match-count contract - three `sed -i` sites including this repo's own release flow at `rad/dev:84`; `calc-cli/dev:57-62,71-76` is a six-line verify dance because `sed` exits 0 whether or not it matched
- `setdefault` / `get_or_insert` - four sites in `ssu` and `ssu2`
- `home_dir()`, `write_file(..., executable=true)`, symlink info in `get_path` (no equivalent of `test -L`), `find_paths(type="dir")` (`cct:127-134` stats every entry)
- binary-file hashing - `hash()` is str-only, so `read_file` plus `hash` covers text only (#153 Tier 3)

Group-by and aggregation (`group_by`, `sum_by`, map-from-parallel-lists, map comprehensions) show up at `posmovements:95-99`, `posbal:70-74`, `argustemp:29-35`, `argus:199-215`, but that's a design conversation rather than a batch item.

---

### Orientation

- Every entry on this list that is genuinely a *new function* follows one flow. Learn it once:
  1. Write `docs/funcs/<name>.md` per the contract in `docs/funcs/README.md`. The `## Signature` line **is** the type-checker's signature - there is no Go-side declaration. Required sections, in order: `# <fn>`, description, `## Signature`, `## Parameters`, `## Examples`, `## Category`.
  2. `make generate` - regenerates `rts/signatures_gen.go`, `rts/embedded_funcs/`, `rts/embedded/functions.txt` (via `function-metadata/extract.go`, which exists because rts cannot import core), and `docs-web/docs/reference/functions.md`.
  3. Add the `FUNC_X` name const and the `BuiltInFunc{Name, Execute}` registration in `core/funcs.go`. Anything non-trivial gets its own `core/func_<name>.go` - see `core/func_matches.go` for a small one, `core/func_parse_date.go` for one returning a map.
  4. Add snapshot cases under `core/testing/snapshots/functions/`.
- All IO and environment access goes through the injectable globals in `core/global.go` (`RIo`, `RClock`, `RShell`, `RReq`, `RExit`, ...). Interpreter code must not call `os.*` / `time.*` / `exec.*` directly - it breaks the end-to-end tests in `core/testing/`, which inject fakes and run the real runner.
- Platform branches belong in `core/common/platform.go`. No scattered `runtime.GOOS` checks. Paths returned to user code are normalized to forward slashes via `NormalizePath`.

### Watch out for

Do not land twenty functions in one change. Each signature is a permanent contract the checker, LSP hover, and docs all inherit, and a wrong parameter name is a breaking change to fix later. Batch by category - paths, temp files, collections, math - and ship each batch on its own, so a bad shape can be caught while it is still cheap.

Group-by and aggregation (`group_by`, `sum_by`, map comprehensions) are explicitly out of scope per the card - they are a design conversation, not a batch item.
title: Fill the stdlib gaps that scripts shell out for
